items.title: Full audit of speed, reliability and code health
items.detail: Twelve simulated years across three test worlds: every dollar accounted for on every day, with no crashes or broken numbers.

items.title: Saves reload exactly
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. Loading a save no longer changes what happens next; it used to shift prices, deliveries and rivals' money.

items.title: Top speed holds five game days a second
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. Late in a game it used to slip to about 4.5, losing time at every month end.

items.title: Game days run about twice as fast
items.detail: 1.76 times faster in v0.30.4. Top speed already holds, so the rest waits until it is needed.

items.title: Month ends as quick as an ordinary day
items.detail: A month end still takes several times as long as an ordinary day. The game now catches up straight after it.

items.title: Faster loading
items.detail: A game takes about nine seconds to open today.

items.title: Split the daily simulation into smaller named steps
items.detail: Makes future changes safer. Nothing a player would notice.

items.title: Marketing screen: campaigns city by city
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. Choose a budget and an agency for each brand in each city, with a 12-month forecast.

items.title: A known brand lets shops charge more
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. From 5% for food up to 30% for jewelry at full awareness; the price cap rises with it.

items.title: Awareness belongs to each city and fades without upkeep
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. About 5% a month, with sales keeping a little of it alive.

items.title: Rivals advertise by the same rules
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. They start from zero and buy campaigns only when it pays. In three test years none has yet, as rivals mostly sell food.

items.title: Automated business playtesting
items.detail: Test companies play 36-month campaigns across shops, factories, mines and supply chains, and balance changes are measured with them.

items.title: Rivals send offers when their supply deals renew
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4. A mine or factory also shows who buys its goods and the price that would win them.

items.title: Suppliers promise only what they can deliver
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4, with fair limits on agreements that go unused or end early.

items.title: Factories show which input limits them
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4, in the Stocking wizard.

items.title: Two free shop lots in every town centre
items.detail: Released in v0.30.4, for new games.

items.title: A well-run shop repays in 8 to 12 years
items.detail: Shops cost a third as much in v0.30.4. In testing a staple shop repays in about 13 years, or about 8 if it signs supply after opening prices fall. It was 35.

items.title: Longer supply chains pay their way
items.detail: In testing, chains repay in about 40 to 50 years, down from over 100.

items.title: Mines and factories win steady buyers
items.detail: Rival offers and winning prices are in v0.30.4. Test companies still get few offers, so this stays open.

items.title: Every founder has a real trade-off, sized from test runs
items.detail: A first pass shipped in v0.30.2. The full pass comes later.

items.title: Opening prices closer to where they settle
items.detail: Prices start about 30% above where they settle, so a first-month agreement locks in a high price.

items.title: One clear typeface and one speed button on every screen
items.detail: Released in v0.30.2.

items.title: Contracts as one tidy list
items.detail: Released in v0.30.3.

items.title: A clearer first hour
items.detail: Price hints and a movable checklist are in. Suggested starter products for each city are still to come.

items.title: Better controls on small screens
items.detail: Phones got a fitted money bar and tidier panels in v0.30.2. Crowded windows are still being simplified.

items.title: Port imports and exports
items.detail: Limited trade through ports that adds to local suppliers rather than replacing them. Ports are not active in the game today.

items.title: Government supply tenders
items.detail: Public supply contracts that companies compete to win.

items.title: Electricity, gas and water providers
items.detail: More detailed utility providers, with commercial bills for the companies that use them.

items.title: Population and household income
items.detail: Closer links between how many people live in a city and what households can spend.

items.title: Inflation and banking
items.detail: Prices and lending tied more closely to the wider economy.

items.title: Research returns
items.detail: Research is switched off for now, and products arrive by year. It comes back once the core business balance is stronger.

items.title: Historical and random crises
items.detail: Optional shocks, real or invented, that test a business in different ways.

items.title: Trade policies
items.detail: Optional rules on trade that change what pays.

items.title: Scenarios
items.detail: Optional set challenges that start a business in a particular situation.

items.title: More of real Baku
items.detail: More of the city's real buildings, painted from photographs.

items.title: Build landmarks as wonders
items.detail: Very expensive and unlocked late, paid in cash or saved up for over time.

items.title: Rivals cannot rush a wonder
items.detail: Rivals start rich, so they follow the same unlock rules and hold no wonders at the start of a game.

items.title: Wonders draw visitors
items.detail: More street life and traffic around them, and more customers for nearby shops.

items.title: Vehicles that turn along curves and roundabouts
items.detail: Needs diagonal vehicle paintings.

items.title: Mansard apartment blocks
items.detail: New paintings for denser, taller city centres.

items.title: A second look at desert colours
items.detail: Deserts were left for later when the foothills were repainted.
